decisions.reason: The same source message directly establishes the corresponding footer codes, and that decision is already fully represented by the candidate's message-59 INTRODUCE Event.
The report-detail identifiers are a separate correction already fully represented by the candidate's message-59 INTRODUCE Event; the header-identifier change adds nothing further.
The risk-band title correction is independent of the header identifiers and is already fully represented by the candidate's message-59 INTRODUCE Event.
Correcting identifiers within existing variants does not change the required DX17–DX20 variant set, its editability, or its selection basis.
The source corrects variant-specific codes displayed in headers but does not alter the separate header presentation, coverage, or space-efficiency requirements.
Correcting report codes does not change the approved visual direction, reference-based theme, or finish priorities.
The variant header-code correction does not change the front-page score panel, result fields, heading, or prominence.
The correction supplies proper report identifiers for specific variants but does not change which customer fields must be editable or their editability standard.
The source does not change the content, format, or detail level of the front-page result drivers.
The source does not change the requirement for consistent footer presence or footer fields; variant-specific footer-code values are already owned by the dedicated footer-identifier Requirement.
Report variant codes are distinct from the vehicle group or assessed-vehicle display, so its content and presentation remain unchanged.
Correcting identifiers in report content does not alter the required fonts, icons, design assets, or delivery package.
